articles.title: ‘The hand of god’ and all that: Lineker, Shilton et al look back at 1986 England-Argentina clash – The Match review
articles.summary: Argentinian co-directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco work hard to appear impartial in account that situates the game in a long continuum of conflict. Here is a football documentary that is a cut above the drain-clogging content that loiters in streaming platforms everywhere.
body: Over and above football matters, it’s clear to see that there were bigger things at stake. Rather obviously, it happened only four years after the Falklands war, which thoroughly poisoned already tense relations between Britain and Argentina. The Match situates the 1986 clash as part of a continuum of strife, dating back at least to the arrival in 1765 of a British sea captain, John Byron, on the Falklands to claim them for Britain. Other key moments: Argentina’s Antonio Rattín getting sent off during the 1966 World Cup, and Maradona being invited on stage by Queen to sing Another One Bites the Dust during their mammoth 1981 South American tour.

articles.title: NFL legend John Madden’s unlikely, unfiltered brilliance: ‘Coach was indeed animated’
articles.summary: With the release of a new David O Russell biopic about the coach turned commentator turned gaming icon, those who knew him best remember his singular career. Wearing his Oakland Raiders uniform and helmet, and gripping an orange traffic cone like a lance, Ted Hendricks rode into the training…
body: “We needed some relief from the intense grind,” recalls Hendricks, 79, who had borrowed the horse from a nearby stable. “It was a spur of the moment idea, but put a smile on everyone’s face. All Coach said once I dismounted was, ‘All right guys, Ted’s here, let’s get started.’ But I know he got a kick out of it too – just from the look on his face and the comments he made later in interviews.”

Madden is fondly and indelibly remembered by his former players, fans who relished his TV commentaries and a generation who grew up playing his eponymous video game. That sets a high bar for the actor Nicolas Cage who, with the help of silicone prosthetics, plays him in a new biopic co-starring Christian Bale, Kathryn Hahn, Sienna Miller, John Mulaney and Shane Gillis, directed ‌by David O Russell.

articles.title: Candle Media’s Kevin Mayer Says ‘Urge to Merge’ Will Last Several Years as Revenue Growth Stalls
articles.summary: If there is one thing Candle Media founder Kevin Mayer understands, it is mergers. The exec oversaw Disney’s 2019 acquisition of 21st Century Fox during his term as the company’s chief strategy officer, where he was also involved in Disney’s acquisition of Pixar, Marvel, Lucasfilm and BAMTech.
body: “You see NBCUniversal not only being split off of Comcast but itself being split between cable networks and the rest of the studio and the rest of the streaming business,” he added. “Those splits are intended to ultimately lead to consolidation of those two companies with other companies. So you are seeing this urge to merge driven by basic financial dynamics, and that is: when growth slows, you want to take that revenue base and amortize it over a smaller cost base.” This movement, Mayer added, will be an “ongoing process for the next several years.”

Still weighing in on Hollywood’s merger fever, Mayer looked back at his own experience at Disney, noting how “easy” it is to “mess up an acquisition.” Bringing two companies together is a process that needs to be done “very carefully,” he said, recalling when Disney bought Pixar from under the realm of former CEO Steve Jobs in 2006.

“Jobs was a very loud voice on this one,” he noted, going on to tell the audience how, from his very first meeting with the Apple founder, former Disney CEO Bob Iger went straight into ironing out how to avoid the possible “cultural issues” of the merger.

articles.title: ‘My body started consuming itself. I was a millimetre from death’: Andrey Zvyagintsev on Covid, Putin and life in exile
articles.summary: The Russian film-maker spent 40 days in a coma and suffered 92% lung damage during the pandemic. He describes how making new movie Minotaur helped his rehabilitation. Andrey Zvyagintsev tells the tale of a knight who is riding through a dark forest and sees a stone sign at a fork in the road.
body: Terrible things tend to happen, that’s the way the world works, and a person is defined by how they respond to each challenge. That goes for the knight in the forest and the characters in a film. It probably goes for Zvyagintsev, too, who has lost not his horse but his home and very nearly his life. The Russian director almost died during the Covid-19 pandemic and spent 40 days in an induced coma. He now lives in exile as an enemy of the state. “I’m with the birds,” he says by way of explaining his situation. “Birds have no borders. They’re not thinking about tomorrow.”

Zvyagintsev’s new film, Minotaur, is a mighty, mesmerising drama of personal and political corruption that has Ukraine as its touchstone, or perhaps its dark fork in the road. He makes no bones about his opposition to the war. Taking the stage at this year’s Cannes film festival, where Minotaur won the grand jury prize, he called on Vladimir Putin to “stop this butchery”, adding that “the whole world is waiting”. In September Russia named him as a “foreign agent” spreading disinformation. He now risks arrest and imprisonment if he dares to go home.

articles.title: Kieran Culkin Says He’s Reuniting With ‘Succession’ Creator Jesse Armstrong on New Movie
articles.summary: Kieran Culkin has let slip that he’s reuniting with Jesse Armstrong for the first time since “Succession” came to an end three years ago — but that it’s got nothing to do with Roman Roy. “I’m about to work with Jesse on a movie — he wrote something,” he told the U.K.’s Heart Breakfast radio on
body: Since losing out in the battle for Waystar at the end of “Succession” and saying goodbye to his Emmy-winning spell as the Roy family’s most foul-mouthed and emotionally chaotic heir, Culkin has become a major movie force. He won the best supporting Oscar for Jesse Eisenberg’s “A Real Pain” and is currently in cinemas as the younger Caesar Flickerman for franchise prequel “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.” Next year, he’s due to appear in Warner Bros.’ untitled Nancy Meyers rom-com alongside Erin Doherty and Jude Law.

For all his move into starry, studio tentpoles, “Succession” fans will likely relish the chance to see Culkin back with the writer who gave him his most memorable role, a role he said he himself missed.

“It was a great show. I miss that whole thing,” he said. “It was a lot of fun because I decided early on, this is a guy who’s never had to suffer consequences in his life. He can just talk his way in and out of any situation, like how fun is that to play! Completely unhinged.”
Returning to what he told Variety in an interview in 2023, Culkin also noted that Armstrong had discussed another season of “Succession” with him.

articles.title: ‘The Big Boom!’: Doc About a Bulgarian Village With a Massive Weapons Factory ‘Anticipates the Future World We’ll Inhabit’
articles.summary: IDFA Frontlight title “The Big Boom!” is rife with contrasts. The fifth documentary from Swiss filmmaker Gabriel Tejedor (“Svetlana: My Father is J. Stalin”) is set in Kazanlak, Bulgaria’s Valley of Roses, where the sounds of explosions often disrupt an otherwise peaceful village.
body: For many residents, the overriding question is how to reconcile this multi-billion-dollar business and the jobs it generates and a brutal war that has devastated lives, homes and communities.

“It’s sad to say but thanks to this war we live very well,” says one resident. “Arsenal guarantees me job security and peace of mind,” says another. Meanwhile, a group of pacifists stage a protest against a monument to a historical figure responsible for the deaths of thousands of Bulgarians.
Given Kazanlak’s deep historical and cultural ties to Russia, many of them harbor mixed feelings about the country their work now opposes.

articles.title: Steps review – Netflix’s Disney-lite Cinderella rework has enough pep in its step
articles.summary: The plot might be a little overstuffed and the animation style could be a little more distinctive, but this is better than the streamer’s average animated offering. Stop me if you’ve heard this one before, but that age-old story you think you know, well, you might not know it at all.
body: While the existence of yet another rule-rewriting storybook rework might not be a surprise, the fact that Steps is mostly rather watchable actually is. It’s not just because of the low bar set by this particular subgenre but also by the streamer’s animated output thus far. Too much of it feels like either off-brand Disney or knock-off DreamWorks, from Spellbound to Swapped to In Your Dreams, and while Steps doesn’t entirely avoid that same trap, its lack of originality is made up for by just about enough pep.

articles.title: Percy Jackson returns as teen stars adapt to life in the limelight
articles.summary: Percy Jackson's lead Walker Scobell admits there are ups and downs to fame as the series returns.
body: Percy Jackson is no ordinary teenager - and neither is the actor tasked with bringing the character to life.
As the son of Greek god Poseidon, Percy has demigod status in the hit Disney series and while Walker Scobell doesn't have his powers, that hasn't made the actor's career any less special.
The TV series, based on the novels by Rick Riordan, sets figures from Greek mythology and their children in the modern day and returns on Friday for its third instalment - The Titan's Curse.
Scobell was 14 when he made his debut as Percy in 2023. Now 17, the US actor says growing up in the spotlight has been an adventure in itself.

articles.title: Babydoll singer Jamie Miller covers Christmas classic
articles.summary: It's Beginning To Look A Lot Like Christmas for the number one hitmaker from Cardiff.
body: After spending four weeks at number one in the UK singles charts, Jamie Miller is releasing his take on the festive classic It's Beginning To Look A Lot Like Christmas.
In October, Miller became the first artist from Wales to top the UK singles chart since 2011 with his TikTok-viral song Babydoll.
The success transformed Miller's career, but he revealed that his "made it" moment was telling his taxi driver dad and cleaner mum they could retire.
While Babydoll's popularity continues, Miller teased the release of his next track on social media, telling fans: "You guys asked for a Christmas song..."

articles.title: Social Media Bans in Tallinn Focus: Should Film Studios and Marketers Panic?
articles.summary: A National Research Group expert shared data on the impact of Australia's social media ban on movie-going among young audiences and discussed the planned U.K. launch of a similar initiative.
body: Australia has banned social media for people under the age of 16. A similar ban is set to hit the U.K. in 2027. And the European Union is talking about potential similar initiatives. So what is the impact on the film industry?

Given all these questions, the Just Film Industry Days program of the Industry@Tallinn & Baltic Event (ITBE) market featured a well-attended Friday session entitled “The New Underground: Film Discovery in the Age of Social Media Restrictions.”

Fergus Navaratnam-Blair, a researcher covering trends in media, entertainment, and technology who manages thought leadership for National Research Group, said that the U.K. social media restrictions would be “more far-reaching” than the ones in Australia.
